beats.say: Kafka is a distributed log. Producers append events to it, and consumers read them whenever they like.

beats.text: A topic is an append-only log. Each event has an offset.
beats.say: Events are stored in a topic, which is an append-only log. Every event gets a number called an offset.

beats.text: Consumers track their own offset. Reading deletes nothing.
beats.say: Consumers keep track of their own position, the offset, and read at their own pace. Reading never deletes anything, so many consumers can read the same data.

beats.text: Partitions: scale the log across brokers.
beats.say: To scale, a topic is split into partitions, spread across brokers. Each partition is its own ordered log.

beats.text: The key picks the partition. Same key, same order.
beats.say: The event key decides the partition, so all events for the same key land in the same partition, and stay in order.

beats.text: Replicated. Kept for the retention period.
beats.say: Partitions are replicated across brokers, and events are kept for a retention period, not until they are read.

beats.say: Next up, consumer groups. Follow for more system design.
